events.title: Rider Advocate brief: 6 claims (0 void)
events.body:
C1: The driver never reached the pickup point: his closest approach was 2137 m away at 21:32:55, and the GPS record shows he never came within 200 m of the pickup at any time. [F1] [NS-1]
C2: No arrival confirmation exists on the timeline: driver_arrived_at is null and the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and the platform recorded no automatic arrival, so NS-1 (i) is not satisfied. [F3 F4] [NS-1 NS-2]
C3: Because the driver was never within the pickup radius, NS-1 (ii) also fails — the driver cannot have been "at the pick-up location according to GPS data" — so the $6.61 cancellation fee is not chargeable to the rider. [F1 F3] [NS-1 NS-2]
C4: The driver himself told the rider at 21:31 that he was still "About 5 min" away, which is consistent with the GPS record that he was over 2 km out; the rider's cancellation at 21:33:20 was therefore not a no-show by the rider. [F8 F1 F2] [NS-1 NS-2]
C5: The $6.61 cancellation fee was actually charged (fare fact) and while the fee stands we should note the rider's own record is clean — 3.4-year account, 4.9 rating, no disputes in 90 days — supporting a straight full refund rather than any account action against the rider. [F5 F2 F14] [NS-2 NS-7]
C6: The driver's account already carries 1 upheld no-show dispute in the last 90 days alongside 2 disputes total, so a second unfounded arrival/cancellation episode warrants sending his account to Ryde for review as an additional action. [F15 F1 F4] [NS-2 RD-6]
Weaknesses: The rider cancelled at 21:33:20, i.e. 3 min 20 s after acceptance — 20 seconds past the 3-minute mark — so under NS-4 (cancelled_by = rider, instant booking, more than 3 minutes after matching) the $6.61 fee is prima facie chargeable unless the NS-1/NS-2 no-show branch is applied. The rider must rely on the fact that the fee here was levied as a driver-claimed no-show, which the system records (F1, F3, F4) refute, rather than on a free-cancellation right; the other side will cite F2 (cancellation 3 min 20 s after acceptance) for NS-4. | The policy contains no rule that the driver arriving late frees the rider from the cancellation fee (NS-8 is expressly not citable), so my client's fairness argument about the driver being far away has no direct clause behind it and I must route it through the missing NS-1 preconditions (F1, F3, F4). | The driver's written statement (F10) that he "was on his way" is not contradicted on its face — a driver 2137 m out is indeed on his way — so I cannot show bad faith from the statement itself; I can only show the objective arrival preconditions fail.
Asks: refund_full $6.61

Because the driver was never within the pickup radius, NS-1 (ii) also fails — the driver cannot have been "at the pick-up location according to GPS data" — so the $6.61 cancellation fee is not chargeable to the rider.

The driver himself told the rider at 21:31 that he was still "About 5 min" away, which is consistent with the GPS record that he was over 2 km out; the rider's cancellation at 21:33:20 was therefore not a no-show by the rider.

The $6.61 cancellation fee was actually charged (fare fact) and while the fee stands we should note the rider's own record is clean — 3.4-year account, 4.9 rating, no disputes in 90 days — supporting a straight full refund rather than any account action against the rider.

weaknesses: The rider cancelled at 21:33:20, i.e. 3 min 20 s after acceptance — 20 seconds past the 3-minute mark — so under NS-4 (cancelled_by = rider, instant booking, more than 3 minutes after matching) the $6.61 fee is prima facie chargeable unless the NS-1/NS-2 no-show branch is applied. The rider must rely on the fact that the fee here was levied as a driver-claimed no-show, which the system records (F1, F3, F4) refute, rather than on a free-cancellation right; the other side will cite F2 (cancellation 3 min 20 s after acceptance) for NS-4.

claims.assertion: The rider's own cancellation is the only cancellation on record: the rider cancelled at 21:33:20, 3 min 20 s after acceptance at 21:30:00, and the $6.61 cancellation fee was charged on that basis (F2, F5).

Because the cancellation was made by the rider more than 3 minutes after matching (3:20 > 3:00), the $6.61 cancellation fee is chargeable under the instant-booking branch of the cancellation policy, which is the only route by which this fee can arise (F2, F5).

There is no record of any arrival confirmation, so the driver never asserted arrival at the pickup point and no waiting-time fee or no-show declaration was imposed; the contested $6.61 is the rider-cancellation fee alone (F3, F4, F5).

The driver informed the rider in-app at 21:31 that he was about 5 minutes away and attributed the delay to traffic, so the rider cancelled with knowledge of the driver's actual position rather than being left uninformed (F8, F2).

The rider's stated reason (the driver was still far away after more than 3 minutes) is a dissatisfaction-with-ETA reason: Ryde publishes no rule that a driver behind the app's ETA gives the rider a free cancellation, and the policy's own information note records that the dataset has no ETA field at all, so no ETA-based waiver can be computed (F1, F2).

The rider's remedy for a fee she considers unfair is the RydeHELP fee-waiver route within 30 days of the trip, not a re-characterisation of the fee as a no-show fee; the cancellation here was not a no-show cancellation and the no-show requirements were never invoked (F3, F4, F5).

Nothing in the record supports a mis-use of the arrival or waiting-fee button: no 'I'm Here' tap exists, so the fraud limb that would attach to a false arrival tap is not engaged and no account flag is warranted on that basis (F3, F4).

Fair-weather conditions (0.0 mm rain, Fair) and the only recorded speed band near the route being 50-59 km/h mean the driver's 5-minute estimate to a pickup 2137 m away was consistent with normal running conditions and the rider's complaint gives no ground for treating the delay as the driver's fault (F1, F8, F11, F13).

The driver's 5.4-year account, 4.61 rating and 409 trips in 90 days are consistent with an ordinary accepted-then-cancelled-on rider booking; the single prior upheld no-show dispute in his history cannot decide this case, which is a rider cancellation, not a no-show (F15, F2).

weaknesses: F1 is the rider's strongest fact: the driver's closest approach was 2137 m at 21:32:55 and he never came within 200 m, so the rider genuinely had no driver nearby; the rider will pair this with her complaint that she was "still far away after more than 3 minutes" to argue the fee is unfair. I cannot rebut the fact, only the legal consequence (NS-4 supplies no ETA-based waiver).

F8 cuts both ways: the driver told the rider "About 5 min, traffic" at 21:31, yet a 5-minute estimate from a 2.1 km position implied arrival around 21:36, after the rider's 21:33:20 cancellation — the rider will argue the driver effectively told her he would not make it and that the promise was never kept.

The traffic facts (F11, F12) show band 6 at 50-59 km/h on Pasir Panjang Drive 3 and no incidents at all, so the driver's "traffic" explanation in F8 is not corroborated by any traffic record; only weather (F13) is favourable, and that does not explain the delay.

The driver never tapped "I'm Here" (F4) and was never within the pickup radius (F1, F3), so the record shows he was simply not at the pickup point 3 min 20 s in — the rider will characterise this as inadequate service, even though under NS-4 that does not by itself shift the fee.

The driver's file has 2 disputes with 1 upheld in the last 90 days, including a no-show dispute (F15), which the rider's side can use to suggest a pattern, and which is a flag_account risk if any fee is found unearned.

events.title: Rider Advocate rebuttal: 9 points
events.body:
→ D1: Accepted as to the mechanics — the rider cancelled at 21:33:20 and $6.61 was charged (F2, F5) — but D1's premise that the rider-cancellation branch is 'the only' route is false: NS-0 routes a fee only through its own branches, and a fee levied on a driver-claimed no-show is judged under NS-1/NS-2, which the system record here defeats because no arrival was ever recorded (F3, F4) and the driver never came within 2137 m of the pickup. [F2 F5 F3 F4 F1] [NS-0 NS-1 NS-2]
→ D2: Contested: the 3-minute rule in NS-4 governs a rider who simply changes her mind, not one who cancels because the driver had not arrived and had not confirmed arrival; NS-1 (i) and (ii) both fail on the record (F3, F4, F1), and NS-2 expressly states that when any of those requirements is unmet the $6.61 is refunded in full. [F3 F4 F1 F2] [NS-4 NS-1 NS-2]
→ D3: I agree the record shows no arrival confirmation and no waiting-fee button (F4), but that cuts for my client, not against her: NS-1 requires the driver to have pressed 'I'm Here' or to have been automatically confirmed at the pickup, so with driver_arrived_at null (F3) there is no valid basis on which the $6.61 can be retained. [F3 F4 F1] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D4: The driver's own message (F8) is a statement, and it is contradicted by the system record: his closest approach was 2137 m at 21:32:55 (F1), so his "About 5 min" at 21:31 implied arrival around 21:36 — after the rider's 21:33:20 cancellation (F2) — meaning the rider cancelled on accurate knowledge that he would not arrive. [F8 F1 F2] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D5 (concedes): Conceded only in the narrow sense that Ryde publishes no ETA-based waiver clause and I do not rely on one; my claim is not that lateness waives the fee but that the fee's factual preconditions were never met (F1, F3, F4). [F1 F3 F4] [NS-1 NS-2]
→ D6: Contested: NS-7's 30-day RydeHELP route is a procedural remedy, not a bar to this adjudication, and NS-2 is the clause that fixes the outcome when NS-1's preconditions fail (F3, F4, F1). [F3 F4 F1 F5] [NS-2 NS-7]
→ D7: I do not allege a false arrival tap; my flag_account request rests on the driver's profile showing 2 disputes with 1 upheld no-show in the last 90 days (F15), which is a permissible additional action and not the basis of the finding itself. [F15 F3 F4] [RD-6 NS-2]
→ D8: Fair weather (F13) does not explain the delay, and the traffic record in fact contradicts the driver's "traffic" excuse: the only band near the route is band 6, 50–59 km/h (F11), with no incidents at all (F12) — so his own explanation for being 2137 m out at 21:32:55 (F1) is uncorroborated by the traffic facts RD-4 requires. [F13 F11 F12 F1 F8] [RD-4 NS-1 NS-2]
→ D9: The driver's tenure and trip count do not cure the failed NS-1 preconditions (F3, F4, F1); the profile is not used to decide the case, only to support the accompanying account-review request (F15). [F15 F3 F4] [NS-1 RD-6]
Revised ask: refund_full $6.61

points.response: Accepted as to the mechanics — the rider cancelled at 21:33:20 and $6.61 was charged (F2, F5) — but D1's premise that the rider-cancellation branch is 'the only' route is false: NS-0 routes a fee only through its own branches, and a fee levied on a driver-claimed no-show is judged under NS-1/NS-2, which the system record here defeats because no arrival was ever recorded (F3, F4) and the driver never came within 2137 m of the pickup.

Contested: the 3-minute rule in NS-4 governs a rider who simply changes her mind, not one who cancels because the driver had not arrived and had not confirmed arrival; NS-1 (i) and (ii) both fail on the record (F3, F4, F1), and NS-2 expressly states that when any of those requirements is unmet the $6.61 is refunded in full.

I agree the record shows no arrival confirmation and no waiting-fee button (F4), but that cuts for my client, not against her: NS-1 requires the driver to have pressed 'I'm Here' or to have been automatically confirmed at the pickup, so with driver_arrived_at null (F3) there is no valid basis on which the $6.61 can be retained.

The driver's own message (F8) is a statement, and it is contradicted by the system record: his closest approach was 2137 m at 21:32:55 (F1), so his "About 5 min" at 21:31 implied arrival around 21:36 — after the rider's 21:33:20 cancellation (F2) — meaning the rider cancelled on accurate knowledge that he would not arrive.

Conceded only in the narrow sense that Ryde publishes no ETA-based waiver clause and I do not rely on one; my claim is not that lateness waives the fee but that the fee's factual preconditions were never met (F1, F3, F4).

I do not allege a false arrival tap; my flag_account request rests on the driver's profile showing 2 disputes with 1 upheld no-show in the last 90 days (F15), which is a permissible additional action and not the basis of the finding itself.

Fair weather (F13) does not explain the delay, and the traffic record in fact contradicts the driver's "traffic" excuse: the only band near the route is band 6, 50–59 km/h (F11), with no incidents at all (F12) — so his own explanation for being 2137 m out at 21:32:55 (F1) is uncorroborated by the traffic facts RD-4 requires.
The driver's tenure and trip count do not cure the failed NS-1 preconditions (F3, F4, F1); the profile is not used to decide the case, only to support the accompanying account-review request (F15).

what_would_change: Had the rider cancelled within 3 minutes of matching, NS-4 would have waived the $6.61 fee.

claims.assertion: The driver never reached the pickup point: his closest approach was 2137 m away at 21:32:55, and the GPS record shows he never came within 200 m of the pickup at any time.
No arrival confirmation exists on the timeline: driver_arrived_at is null and the driver never tapped "I'm Here" and the platform recorded no automatic arrival, so NS-1 (i) is not satisfied.

Because the driver was never within the pickup radius, NS-1 (ii) also fails — the driver cannot have been "at the pick-up location according to GPS data" — so the $6.61 cancellation fee is not chargeable to the rider.

The driver himself told the rider at 21:31 that he was still "About 5 min" away, which is consistent with the GPS record that he was over 2 km out; the rider's cancellation at 21:33:20 was therefore not a no-show by the rider.

The $6.61 cancellation fee was actually charged (fare fact) and while the fee stands we should note the rider's own record is clean — 3.4-year account, 4.9 rating, no disputes in 90 days — supporting a straight full refund rather than any account action against the rider.

The driver's account already carries 1 upheld no-show dispute in the last 90 days alongside 2 disputes total, so a second unfounded arrival/cancellation episode warrants sending his account to Ryde for review as an additional action.

weaknesses: The rider cancelled at 21:33:20, i.e. 3 min 20 s after acceptance — 20 seconds past the 3-minute mark — so under NS-4 (cancelled_by = rider, instant booking, more than 3 minutes after matching) the $6.61 fee is prima facie chargeable unless the NS-1/NS-2 no-show branch is applied. The rider must rely on the fact that the fee here was levied as a driver-claimed no-show, which the system records (F1, F3, F4) refute, rather than on a free-cancellation right; the other side will cite F2 (cancellation 3 min 20 s after acceptance) for NS-4.

The policy contains no rule that the driver arriving late frees the rider from the cancellation fee (NS-8 is expressly not citable), so my client's fairness argument about the driver being far away has no direct clause behind it and I must route it through the missing NS-1 preconditions (F1, F3, F4).

The driver's written statement (F10) that he "was on his way" is not contradicted on its face — a driver 2137 m out is indeed on his way — so I cannot show bad faith from the statement itself; I can only show the objective arrival preconditions fail.

claims.assertion: The rider's own cancellation is the only cancellation on record: the rider cancelled at 21:33:20, 3 min 20 s after acceptance at 21:30:00, and the $6.61 cancellation fee was charged on that basis (F2, F5).

Because the cancellation was made by the rider more than 3 minutes after matching (3:20 > 3:00), the $6.61 cancellation fee is chargeable under the instant-booking branch of the cancellation policy, which is the only route by which this fee can arise (F2, F5).

There is no record of any arrival confirmation, so the driver never asserted arrival at the pickup point and no waiting-time fee or no-show declaration was imposed; the contested $6.61 is the rider-cancellation fee alone (F3, F4, F5).

The driver informed the rider in-app at 21:31 that he was about 5 minutes away and attributed the delay to traffic, so the rider cancelled with knowledge of the driver's actual position rather than being left uninformed (F8, F2).

The rider's stated reason (the driver was still far away after more than 3 minutes) is a dissatisfaction-with-ETA reason: Ryde publishes no rule that a driver behind the app's ETA gives the rider a free cancellation, and the policy's own information note records that the dataset has no ETA field at all, so no ETA-based waiver can be computed (F1, F2).

The rider's remedy for a fee she considers unfair is the RydeHELP fee-waiver route within 30 days of the trip, not a re-characterisation of the fee as a no-show fee; the cancellation here was not a no-show cancellation and the no-show requirements were never invoked (F3, F4, F5).

Nothing in the record supports a mis-use of the arrival or waiting-fee button: no 'I'm Here' tap exists, so the fraud limb that would attach to a false arrival tap is not engaged and no account flag is warranted on that basis (F3, F4).

Fair-weather conditions (0.0 mm rain, Fair) and the only recorded speed band near the route being 50-59 km/h mean the driver's 5-minute estimate to a pickup 2137 m away was consistent with normal running conditions and the rider's complaint gives no ground for treating the delay as the driver's fault (F1, F8, F11, F13).

The driver's 5.4-year account, 4.61 rating and 409 trips in 90 days are consistent with an ordinary accepted-then-cancelled-on rider booking; the single prior upheld no-show dispute in his history cannot decide this case, which is a rider cancellation, not a no-show (F15, F2).

weaknesses: F1 is the rider's strongest fact: the driver's closest approach was 2137 m at 21:32:55 and he never came within 200 m, so the rider genuinely had no driver nearby; the rider will pair this with her complaint that she was "still far away after more than 3 minutes" to argue the fee is unfair. I cannot rebut the fact, only the legal consequence (NS-4 supplies no ETA-based waiver).

F8 cuts both ways: the driver told the rider "About 5 min, traffic" at 21:31, yet a 5-minute estimate from a 2.1 km position implied arrival around 21:36, after the rider's 21:33:20 cancellation — the rider will argue the driver effectively told her he would not make it and that the promise was never kept.

The traffic facts (F11, F12) show band 6 at 50-59 km/h on Pasir Panjang Drive 3 and no incidents at all, so the driver's "traffic" explanation in F8 is not corroborated by any traffic record; only weather (F13) is favourable, and that does not explain the delay.

The driver never tapped "I'm Here" (F4) and was never within the pickup radius (F1, F3), so the record shows he was simply not at the pickup point 3 min 20 s in — the rider will characterise this as inadequate service, even though under NS-4 that does not by itself shift the fee.

The driver's file has 2 disputes with 1 upheld in the last 90 days, including a no-show dispute (F15), which the rider's side can use to suggest a pattern, and which is a flag_account risk if any fee is found unearned.

points.response: Accepted as to the mechanics — the rider cancelled at 21:33:20 and $6.61 was charged (F2, F5) — but D1's premise that the rider-cancellation branch is 'the only' route is false: NS-0 routes a fee only through its own branches, and a fee levied on a driver-claimed no-show is judged under NS-1/NS-2, which the system record here defeats because no arrival was ever recorded (F3, F4) and the driver never came within 2137 m of the pickup.

Contested: the 3-minute rule in NS-4 governs a rider who simply changes her mind, not one who cancels because the driver had not arrived and had not confirmed arrival; NS-1 (i) and (ii) both fail on the record (F3, F4, F1), and NS-2 expressly states that when any of those requirements is unmet the $6.61 is refunded in full.

I agree the record shows no arrival confirmation and no waiting-fee button (F4), but that cuts for my client, not against her: NS-1 requires the driver to have pressed 'I'm Here' or to have been automatically confirmed at the pickup, so with driver_arrived_at null (F3) there is no valid basis on which the $6.61 can be retained.

The driver's own message (F8) is a statement, and it is contradicted by the system record: his closest approach was 2137 m at 21:32:55 (F1), so his "About 5 min" at 21:31 implied arrival around 21:36 — after the rider's 21:33:20 cancellation (F2) — meaning the rider cancelled on accurate knowledge that he would not arrive.

Conceded only in the narrow sense that Ryde publishes no ETA-based waiver clause and I do not rely on one; my claim is not that lateness waives the fee but that the fee's factual preconditions were never met (F1, F3, F4).
Contested: NS-7's 30-day RydeHELP route is a procedural remedy, not a bar to this adjudication, and NS-2 is the clause that fixes the outcome when NS-1's preconditions fail (F3, F4, F1).

I do not allege a false arrival tap; my flag_account request rests on the driver's profile showing 2 disputes with 1 upheld no-show in the last 90 days (F15), which is a permissible additional action and not the basis of the finding itself.

Fair weather (F13) does not explain the delay, and the traffic record in fact contradicts the driver's "traffic" excuse: the only band near the route is band 6, 50–59 km/h (F11), with no incidents at all (F12) — so his own explanation for being 2137 m out at 21:32:55 (F1) is uncorroborated by the traffic facts RD-4 requires.
The driver's tenure and trip count do not cure the failed NS-1 preconditions (F3, F4, F1); the profile is not used to decide the case, only to support the accompanying account-review request (F15).

Accepted as a fact and irrelevant as a conclusion: F1 shows the driver's closest approach was 2137 m at 21:32:55, but NS-1 governs only a driver-claimed no-show cancellation, and no such claim was made here (F4 shows no arrival tap, no automatic arrival).

This point is conceded and it defeats the rider's own case: because NS-1 (i) fails, NS-1 never opens at all, and the fee must therefore be assessed under the only branch the record supports — cancelled_by = rider, 3 min 20 s after acceptance (F2) — which is chargeable under NS-4.

Conceded as to the NS-1 (ii) precondition, but the rider's inference is wrong: NS-1 and NS-2 are the no-show branch, which only applies when the driver cancels claiming a no-show, and here the rider cancelled (F2), so NS-2's refund_full consequence is never triggered and the $6.61 stands under NS-4.

This is the rider's best fairness point and it is still not a defence under the fee rules: the driver's 21:31 message (F8) plus F1 confirm he was over 2 km out, yet Ryde publishes no rule making a driver behind ETA a free-cancellation ground, and the dataset carries no ETA field to compute one, so the remedy for a fee the rider believes unfair is the NS-7 waiver route, not recharacterisation of the fee.

The rider's clean profile (F14) is not in dispute, but profile facts can never decide the fee (they may only support an account action), and the $6.61 is chargeable under NS-4 on the rider's own cancellation at 21:33:20 — 3 min 20 s after matching — so refund_full has no clause behind it.

This request has no basis: no arrival or waiting-fee button was pressed (F4), no arrival was recorded (F3), and the driver did not cancel or claim a no-show (F2), so none of the abuse/flag grounds are engaged; F15's single prior upheld no-show dispute is profile evidence, which cannot alone decide or flag this case, and RD-6 is a route-deviation provision entirely inapplicable to this no-show case.

If you believe the fee is unfair, you can ask for a fee waiver through the RydeHELP fee-waiver option within 30 days of the trip; Ryde decides those case by case.
